Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need.

Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

Precourt Institute for Energy

As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability , the Precourt Institute for Energy concentrates the talents of the University on energy research and education, from basic science and technology to policy and business. Our mission is to spark the creativity, collaboration, learning, and leadership needed for the global energy transformation. The initiatives, research centers, and educational programs of the Precourt Institute connect across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools supporting work with the potential to solve the toughest energy challenges from science and engineering to policy and economics. We also build collaborations globally with industry, other research institutions, government, and civic organizations in pursuit of sustainable, affordable, secure energy for all people.

Position Overview

The Precourt Institute for Energy seeks exceptional candidates for the role of Executive Director, Partnerships & Strategy
. Reporting directly to and working closely with the Precourt Institute Director, the Executive Director will spearhead the development and execution of a comprehensive strategy that integrates the academic and practitioner perspectives, capabilities and resources across the research, development and deployment pipeline to advance sustainable, affordable and secure energy for all.

Working with the Institute director, faculty fellows, staff and advisory council, the Executive Director will design and build a cohesive fabric to enable the Institute’s centers, initiative and programs (as well as other units across Stanford) to sustain thriving, multi-faceted partnerships with industry and non-profit organizations. The expected outcome is that Stanford partners with practitioners and delivers research impact across all facets of the energy system such that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.

The role will spearhead the development and growth of large, funded partnerships and alliances with industry and non-profit organizations, by leveraging the breadth and depth of expertise among Stanford faculty and researchers and by coordinating with centers, initiatives and programs in the Institute and with other units across Stanford. The Executive Director will represent the institute in senior-level strategic discussions and engage with energy leaders.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Develop and execute a strategic vision and plan that integrates academic and practitioner perspectives, capabilities and resources to advance Stanford’s mission across the entire energy system.
Create and strengthen connective tissues to bring together specific domains of energy research through strategic convenings and grantmaking.
Deliver significant funded partnerships between Stanford, industry and non-profit organizations.
Coordinate with centers, initiatives program and stakeholders across Stanford to catalyze research and partnerships that spans all facets of energy.
Lead and manage a team supporting complex energy research programs and partnerships, including technical experts and professionals responsible for partnership development, faculty engagement, grantmaking, and program execution.
Ensure successful execution of funded programs by monitoring progress, managing risks, and maintaining accountability for sponsor expectations and contractual commitments.
Serve as a senior liaison to management, cross-functional areas, schools, sponsors, and other external organizations.

In addition to the minimum qualifications listed below, our preferred qualifications include:

PhD degree and 15 years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience. Advanced degree may be required.
Exceptional understanding of the energy technology ecosystem.
Exceptional communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders, including senior government officials and corporate executives.
Strategic thinker with the ability to connect technological innovation with economic and policy considerations.
Demonstrated ability to identify, develop, and cultivate strategic partnerships across academia, industry, and government.
Proven ability to resolve complex issues quickly and make sound decisions that advance university objectives within a collaborative culture.

The expected pay range for this position is $214,936 to $260,287 per annum.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Who We Are

The Chicago Cultural Alliance (CCA) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. Our mission is to connect, promote, and support centers of cultural heritage for a more inclusive Chicago. We unite over 50 Chicago-area cultural heritage museums, centers, and historical societies that span 23 neighborhoods and 11 suburbs in the Chicago area and represent over 40 different cultures from around the world.

What We Do

Chicago Cultural Alliance (CCA) connects, promotes, and supports its member organizations through programs, events, professional development, networking, and opportunities for collaboration. With a full-time staff of four, CCA works closely with its members, Board, partners, funders, and community stakeholders throughout the Chicago area. CCA’s signature programs and events include Activating Heritage, Journey Chicago, MOSAIC, and World Dumpling Fest. (Descriptions of each are available on the CCA web site.) CCA also provides capacity-building, networking, and professional development opportunities for its members; strengthens connections among member organizations; and develops productive, sustained relationships with funders and community partners.

We are seeking a visionary leader familiar with both the cultural and funding landscape of Chicago, who can lead the organization into its next phase of growth. The next Executive Director for the CCA will serve as a leader for staff and a collaborator with our Board of Directors, a wide network of volunteers, and an impressive collection of core and partner member organizations to realize the mission of the organization. The new ED will expand the organization’s networks to grow the financial support for the organization, both through new revenue and philanthropic giving. The ED will seek to build a supportive, flexible work environment at CCA that will effectively advocate for diverse communities and voices.

Schedule

The CCA team works remotely with one in-office team meeting per week. The executive director is required to attend major programs, including the Annual Meeting of Membership (January), Activating Heritage conference (March), and the MOSAIC fundraiser gala (Spring). This position requires regular travel throughout Chicagoland for donor meetings, events, board engagements, community activities, and partner visits.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of the Chicago Cultural Alliance serves as the chief administrative and executive officer and has primary responsibility for the organization’s financial sustainability, fundraising, operations, external relationships, and continued growth.

This is an external-facing, development-forward leadership opportunity. The Executive Director will inherit a base of philanthropic, corporate, and community relationships, while also having the opportunity to build a more sophisticated and diversified development operation. The successful candidate will personally cultivate relationships with high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners. This is a position ideal for an individual with the ability to strategically maximize the financial resources of the CCA while motivating the staff.

The Executive Director provides overall organizational and operational leadership, overseeing a budget of approximately $700,000 and leading a team of three. The Executive Director will manage organizational priorities, support a talented team, and ensure that revenue growth translates into programmatic growth.

Primary Responsibilities:

●     
 Lead the CCA, responsible for overseeing the administration, fundraising, programs, and strategies of the organization.
●      Work closely with stakeholders to develop and implement a vision for the organization as it evolves.
●      Serve as a bridge-builder, creating an ever-stronger network of cultural heritage organizations and connections for those organizations to government offices, businesses, and foundations/philanthropy.
●       Lead the fundraising and revenue strategy, establishing annual and multi-year goals and personally driving major individual, corporate, foundation, and partnership opportunities.
●      
Build and manage a portfolio of donors and prospects, cultivating high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners and personally soliciting and stewarding major commitments.
●      
Serve as the most visible ambassador for the CCA, representing the organization with donors, corporate and civic leaders, philanthropic institutions, community organizations, media, and other key stakeholders across Chicagoland.
●      Build a strong and connected team culture, providing clear expectations, regular communication and feedback, professional development, accountability, and support while fostering a collaborative, respectful, and inclusive workplace.
●       Partner with and engage the CCA Board of Directors, working closely with the Board President and committee leadership to advance CCA’s strategic priorities. Activate Board members as ambassadors, donors, connectors, event participants, and fundraisers. Board support tasks will include participating in monthly committee meetings, stewardship tasks, and other responsibilities.
●      
Financial stewardship with support from the Finance Committee and an accounting service. Overseeing budgeting, forecasting, revenue performance, and financial decision-making.
●      
Build a strong and connected team culture, providing clarity, accountability, and support while maintaining the collaborative, flexible, and mission-driven culture that characterizes the CCA.
●      
Oversee the three supporting staff positions: Director of Programs, Design & Marketing Manager, and Operations Manager.

Compensation & Benefits

●    
 Salary range: $90,000-$100,00 annually, commensurate with experience. Additionally, the Chicago Cultural Alliance offers medical benefits through United Healthcare (50% employer paid premium).
●     7 paid holidays + paid winter break (Dec. 24 th through January 1 st ).
●     16 days paid time off (accrued).
●     Various professional development opportunities covered by employer (ex. conference attendance, workshops, online workshops, or courses).
●     Satisfying work advocating for Chicago’s centers of cultural heritage.
●     Regularly engaging with colleagues in Chicago’s arts and cultural communities.

Requirements

●     
Demonstrated senior leadership experience in a nonprofit, cultural, philanthropic, community-based, or similarly mission-driven organization, including experience working effectively with a governing board. 3+ years of senior leadership experience preferred.
●     Demonstrated success developing and executing fundraising or revenue-development strategies, including cultivation and stewarding individual, corporate, foundation and/or institutional relationships.
●     Demonstrated experience supervising, developing, and supporting staff and building a collaborative and accountable workplace culture.
●     Candidate must live in the Chicagoland area.
●     Demonstrated ability to lead both strategy and execution in a small or resource-constrained environment.
●     Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
●      Ability to reliably travel throughout the Chicagoland area.
●     
Skill with computer programs including, Google Workspace apps (Google Drive / Docs / Sheets / Slides), Asana, CRM systems (Neon), Zoom, email, and messaging software or similar.
●     All team members of the CCA must follow our organizational mission to support, promote, and advocate for the centers of cultural heritage that we unite. This requires cultural sensitivity, an interest in other cultures, specifically immigrant cultures, advocacy, and related topics. We strongly recommend that applicants review the Chicago Cultural Alliance mission statement before applying.
●     Ability to work both independently and as part of a small, highly collaborative team.
●     Must have regular and reliable access to the Internet.
●     Excellent communication skills, including public speaking and stakeholder engagement.
●      Ability to track, analyze, and use program data to inform decisions and improve outcomes.

How to Apply

If interested, please send a cover letter, CV/résumé (with at least three references)
, and writing sample
addressed to CCA Hiring Committee (careers@chicagoculturalalliance.org) with “CCA Executive Director” as the subject. We ask that cover letters do not exceed 2 pages in length using size 12 font. Suggested writing sample might include a grant proposal, appeal letter, exhibit text, or other public-facing work.

Only complete applications that include a cover letter, CV/résumé (with at least three references), and writing sample will be considered.

Hiring Timeline

Step 1: Select applicants will be invited to schedule a 45-minute Zoom interview.

Step 2: Applicants advancing to the next stage will be invited to an in-person interview with the hiring committee.

Step 3: Interviewers will contact applicant references.

Step 4: CCA Board President will extend a job offer to the best candidate.

All inquiries and discussions will be handled with the utmost confidentiality. Applications will be reviewed immediately upon receipt and on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Chicago Cultural Alliance provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. The National Network of Abortion Funds (NNAF) works to advance the movement for abortion access by investing in its member network of autonomous abortion funds. We aim to strengthen the network by sustainably resourcing abortion funds, amplifying the work of abortion funds across movements, and fortifying the interconnectedness of abortion funds. In so doing, we envision a world where every reproductive decision, including abortion, is fully accessible and free from shame, coercion, political interference, and criminalization. We also envision a world where abortion funds are connected to each other and move in partnership as they create and respond to their local conditions, resources, and communities. In this future, all people have the power and resources to care for and affirm their bodies, communities, and reproductive health, in all areas of their lives. 

We invite you to join us as NNAF's next Executive Director at a pivotal moment for the network. 
NNAF is comprised of a multi-racial, multi-religious, gender expansive staff of 75, located across the United States. We know how important it is to support our remote staff to maintain connection and cohesiveness as a team. To this end, we ensure weekly one-on-one supervision, face-to-face virtual staff meetings, quarterly in-person meetings, and more.

The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for stewarding organizational stability, strategic alignment, and movement leadership at the National Network of Abortion Funds (NNAF), particularly in response to the current political climate.

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors - composed of current and former abortion fund activists and leaders in reproductive and cross-sector social justice - the Executive Director guides strategic decision-making that aligns with NNAF's mission and the evolving needs of network members.
The ED role sits at a unique intersection: serving as the primary external voice and movement leader while maintaining genuine presence and connection with internal teams. The ED works closely with the Managing Director (MD) (who leads internal operations, culture, and day-to-day management) to ensure clear role delineation and coordinated strategy. This role requires someone who can balance bold external presence with humble curiosity about how the organization actually works, and who understands the complex power dynamics among staff, member funds, Board, funders, and movement partners.

The role emphasizes building on existing organizational momentum, ensuring financial sustainability and values-aligned fundraising, and representing NNAF as a stable, visionary leader in the movement for abortion access and reproductive justice. The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. Our mission is to spark the creativity, collaboration, learning, and leadership needed for the global energy transformation. The initiatives, research centers, and educational programs of the Precourt Institute connect across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools supporting work with the potential to solve the toughest energy challenges from science and engineering to policy and economics. We also build collaborations globally with industry, other research institutions, government, and civic organizations in pursuit of sustainable, affordable, secure energy for all people.

. Who We Are

The Chicago Cultural Alliance (CCA) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. Our mission is to connect, promote, and support centers of cultural heritage for a more inclusive Chicago. We unite over 50 Chicago-area cultural heritage museums, centers, and historical societies that span 23 neighborhoods and 11 suburbs in the Chicago area and represent over 40 different cultures from around the world.

What We Do

Chicago Cultural Alliance (CCA) connects, promotes, and supports its member organizations through programs, events, professional development, networking, and opportunities for collaboration. With a full-time staff of four, CCA works closely with its members, Board, partners, funders, and community stakeholders throughout the Chicago area. CCA’s signature programs and events include Activating Heritage, Journey Chicago, MOSAIC, and World Dumpling Fest. (Descriptions of each are available on the CCA web site.) CCA also provides capacity-building, networking, and professional development opportunities for its members; strengthens connections among member organizations; and develops productive, sustained relationships with funders and community partners.

We are seeking a visionary leader familiar with both the cultural and funding landscape of Chicago, who can lead the organization into its next phase of growth. The next Executive Director for the CCA will serve as a leader for staff and a collaborator with our Board of Directors, a wide network of volunteers, and an impressive collection of core and partner member organizations to realize the mission of the organization. The new ED will expand the organization’s networks to grow the financial support for the organization, both through new revenue and philanthropic giving. The ED will seek to build a supportive, flexible work environment at CCA that will effectively advocate for diverse communities and voices.

Schedule

The CCA team works remotely with one in-office team meeting per week. The executive director is required to attend major programs, including the Annual Meeting of Membership (January), Activating Heritage conference (March), and the MOSAIC fundraiser gala (Spring). This position requires regular travel throughout Chicagoland for donor meetings, events, board engagements, community activities, and partner visits.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of the Chicago Cultural Alliance serves as the chief administrative and executive officer and has primary responsibility for the organization’s financial sustainability, fundraising, operations, external relationships, and continued growth.

The Executive Director will inherit a base of philanthropic, corporate, and community relationships, while also having the opportunity to build a more sophisticated and diversified development operation. The successful candidate will personally cultivate relationships with high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners. This is a position ideal for an individual with the ability to strategically maximize the financial resources of the CCA while motivating the staff.

The Executive Director will manage organizational priorities, support a talented team, and ensure that revenue growth translates into programmatic growth.

Build and manage a portfolio of donors and prospects, cultivating high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners and personally soliciting and stewarding major commitments.

●       Partner with and engage the CCA Board of Directors, working closely with the Board President and committee leadership to advance CCA’s strategic priorities. Activate Board members as ambassadors, donors, connectors, event participants, and fundraisers. ●      
Financial stewardship with support from the Finance Committee and an accounting service. Overseeing budgeting, forecasting, revenue performance, and financial decision-making.

Oversee the three supporting staff positions: Director of Programs, Design & Marketing Manager, and Operations Manager.

Skill with computer programs including, Google Workspace apps (Google Drive / Docs / Sheets / Slides), Asana, CRM systems (Neon), Zoom, email, and messaging software or similar.

Big Sky Youth Empowerment (BYEP) is an adventure-based group mentoring program that has served 1,200+ young people in the Gallatin Valley over the past 25 years. GROWMARK also owns and operates SEEDWAY, the largest full-line seed company in the United States. More information is available at growmark.com.

Purpose And Summary Statement

Responsible for the operation and performance of the sales function of the Crop Protection and Seed Divisions across the GROWMARK System. Leads the Crop Protection and Seed sales organization including sales process, tools, training, and incentives to grow seed and crop protection share and net new acres, and deliver profitable growth for GROWMARK and its member companies.

SUPERVISION AND LEADERSHIP

Supervises, leads, and develops the Agronomy Sales and Marketing Directors. Provides functional leadership to FS member company sales leaders and crop specialists, and leads cross-functional initiatives across sales, portfolio marketing, agronomy services, customer care, operations, and technology.

Essential Job Functions

Accountable for seed, seed treatment, and crop protection sales, net new acre, and share targets for the System, and contributes to Seed and Crop Protection divisional income targets.

Develops and implements the System Crop Protection and Seed sales strategy and annual sales plans for all member companies and target markets, aligned with the Seed and Crop Protection strategic plans.

Defines the GROWMARK Crop Protection and Seed sales process and Customer Relationship Management approach, drives CRM adoption, and directs the sales tools, technology, dashboards, and KPIs that support consistent field execution and accountability.

Owns the System approach to account targeting, grower business planning, pipeline management, and customer segmentation, enabling field teams to deliver data-driven, acre-level recommendations and economic value propositions.

Sets acre ownership and account management standards across the System and directs crop specialist and salesperson training at all member companies, including onboarding, consultative selling, product positioning, and the Certified Crop Specialist designation, in coordination with Agronomy Services and Field Training.

Develops and administers sales incentive programs and oversees the application of business builder and market impact funds to align field behavior with strategic priorities.

Partners with the Executive Directors of Seed and Crop Protection Portfolio on grower programs, pricing, product positioning, and new product launch so that portfolio strategy is executed consistently in the field, and integrates seed, crop protection, and agronomic solutions into cohesive, System-based customer offerings.

Drives adoption of myFS Agronomy and related digital agronomy tools as the data foundation for the agronomy sales model.

Leads member company alignment on sales strategy through direct relationships with FS CEO/GMs and agronomy sales and procurement leaders and collaborates with Member Resources to improve earned business among all GROWMARK members.

Develops annual sales forecasts, budgets, and growth targets, monitors financial performance of sales activities, and reports regularly to the VP, Crop Protection and Seed on sales performance, acre and share progress, market opportunities, and financial results.
